dimensions.label: Safe: personal security: visibility, openness, lighting, likelihood of crime or disorder
Lively: vibrancy and activity: people, shops, social interaction, busy street use
Beautiful: visual coherence, attractive architecture, natural elements, overall landscape
Wealthy: economic prosperity: building condition, types of shops, maintenance, visible investment
Depressing: sadness or discomfort from decay, neglect, lack of activity or visual disorder
Boring: lack of stimulation, novelty or diversity; monotony, low activity, uniform forms
Clean: orderliness, hygiene and maintenance; no litter, pollution, graffiti or deterioration

config.description: Method replication: the images are new Baidu street views of the six historic districts in central Shanghai studied by Wang, Zhang & Huang (2025, Sustainability): the Bund, Nanjing West Road, Yuyuan Road, Hengshan Road–Fuxing Road, Shanyin Road and Tilanqiao (one of four directions at each point), not the paper's 3,371 images. Adults rate each view on seven perceptions, safe, lively, beautiful, wealthy, depressing, boring and clean, on a five-point Likert scale, each with the paper's short definition. As in the paper, each participant rates five random views. Differences from the original study: (1) the paper let participants rate only the dimensions they found relevant; here all seven are answered; (2) the districts' sampling areas were drawn by us around each named district.

paper.title: Nonlinear Perceptual Thresholds and Trade-Offs of Visual Environment in Historic Districts: Evidence from Street View Images in Shanghai
